body.en: Trigonometry accounts for 4 to 6 questions on every ACT Math test, heavily concentrated in the challenging final third of the exam (questions 40–60). Mastery requires knowing right-triangle ratios, reciprocal functions, unit-circle angles, sinusoidal wave modeling, and the Laws of Sines and Cosines.
body.ar: حساب المثلثات accounts for 4 to 6 questions on every ACT Math test, heavily concentrated in the challenging final third of the exam (questions 40–60). Mastery requires knowing right-المثلث ratios, reciprocal الدوال, unit-الدائرة angles, sinusoidal wave modeling, and the Laws of Sines and Cosines.

label.en: Definition 6.1 — Right Triangle Ratios & Reciprocal Functions
label.ar: تعريف 6.1 — Right المثلث Ratios & Reciprocal الدوال

body.en:
For an acute angle \(\theta\) in a right triangle with adjacent side \(a\), opposite side \(b\), and hypotenuse \(c\):
  • Primary Trigonometric Ratios:
    \[ \sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{b}{c}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{a}{c}, \quad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = \frac{b}{a} \]
  • Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions (High ACT Frequency):
    \[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{c}{b}, \quad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{c}{a}, \quad \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{a}{b} \]
  • Quotient Identity: \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) and \(\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\).
body.ar:
For an acute الزاوية \(\theta\) in a right المثلث with adjacent side \(a\), opposite side \(b\), and hypotenuse \(c\):
  • Primary Trigonometric Ratios:
    \[ \sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{b}{c}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{a}{c}, \quad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = \frac{b}{a} \]
  • Reciprocal Trigonometric الدوال (High ACT Frequency):
    \[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{c}{b}, \quad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{c}{a}, \quad \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{a}{b} \]
  • Quotient المتطابقة: \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) and \(\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\).

label.en: Theorem 6.1 — Identities, Quadrants, and Non-Right Triangle Laws
label.ar: مبرهنة 6.1 — المتطابقات, Quadrants, and Non-Right المثلث Laws

body.en:
Key formulas required for advanced ACT trigonometry:
  • Pythagorean Identities:
    \[ \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \]\[ 1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta, \quad 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta \]
  • Quadrant Signs (ASTC Rule):
    Quadrant I: All positive (\(A\)).
    Quadrant II: Sine positive, Cosine & Tangent negative (\(S\)).
    Quadrant III: Tangent positive, Sine & Cosine negative (\(T\)).
    Quadrant IV: Cosine positive, Sine & Tangent negative (\(C\)).
  • Sinusoidal Function Modeling: For \(y = A\sin(B(x - C)) + D\) or \(y = A\cos(B(x - C)) + D\):
    \[ \text{Amplitude} = |A|, \quad \text{Period} = \frac{2\pi}{B} \text{ (or } \frac{360^\circ}{B} \text{)}, \quad \text{Midline} = y = D \]
  • Laws of Sines and Cosines (Oblique Triangles): For any triangle with sides \(a, b, c\) opposite angles \(A, B, C\):
    \[ \frac{\sin A}{a} = \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin C}{c} \quad (\text{Law of Sines}) \]\[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C \implies \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \quad (\text{Law of Cosines}) \]

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Mode: The ACT gives problems in both degrees and radians without warning. Ensure your graphing calculator mode matches the problem context before calculating angles or evaluating functions.
  • Reciprocal Name Confusion: Remember that the reciprocal pairs have opposite starting letters: \(\sin\) pairs with \(\mathbf{c}\text{sc}\) (not sec), and \(\cos\) pairs with \(\mathbf{s}\text{ec}\) (not csc).
  • Period of \(y = A\sin(Bx)\): The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{B}\) (or \(\frac{360^\circ}{B}\)), NOT \(2\pi B\). If \(y = 5\sin(4x)\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\), not \(8\pi\).
  • Law of Cosines Negative Sign: The formula is \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\). When \(\angle C\) is obtuse (\(90^\circ < C < 180^\circ\)), \(\cos C < 0\), turning the minus sign into an addition!
body.ar:

label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (حساب المثلثات)

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).
body.ar:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-الصيغة & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-الزاوية المتطابقة gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching المعاملات with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.A — ASTC Signs and Reciprocal Trig Evaluation
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.A — ASTC Signs and Reciprocal Trig Evaluation

body.en:
If \(\cos\theta = -\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2}\), what is the exact value of \(\tan\theta + \csc\theta\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify the quadrant: \(\pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2}\) is Quadrant III.
  2. Recall the signs in Quadrant III (ASTC): \(\sin\theta < 0\), \(\cos\theta < 0\), \(\tan\theta > 0\).
  3. Construct the reference right triangle or use the Pythagorean identity: \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = 1 - \left(-\frac{5}{13}\right)^2 = 1 - \frac{25}{169} = \frac{144}{169}\).
    Since sine is negative in Quadrant III: \(\sin\theta = -\frac{12}{13}\).
  4. Evaluate \(\tan\theta\) and \(\csc\theta\):
    \[ \tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-12/13}{-5/13} = +\frac{12}{5} \]\[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{1}{-12/13} = -\frac{13}{12} \]
  5. Sum the values with a common denominator (\(60\)):
    \[ \tan\theta + \csc\theta = \frac{12}{5} - \frac{13}{12} = \frac{144 - 65}{60} = \frac{79}{60} \]
The exact value is \(\mathbf{\frac{79}{60}}\).
body.ar:
If \(\cos\theta = -\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2}\), what is the exact value of \(\tan\theta + \csc\theta\)?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Identify the quadrant: \(\pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2}\) is Quadrant III.
  2. Recall the signs in Quadrant III (ASTC): \(\sin\theta < 0\), \(\cos\theta < 0\), \(\tan\theta > 0\).
  3. Construct the reference right المثلث or use the Pythagorean المتطابقة: \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = 1 - \left(-\frac{5}{13}\right)^2 = 1 - \frac{25}{169} = \frac{144}{169}\).
    Since sine is negative in Quadrant III: \(\sin\theta = -\frac{12}{13}\).
  4. Evaluate \(\tan\theta\) and \(\csc\theta\):
    \[ \tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-12/13}{-5/13} = +\frac{12}{5} \]\[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{1}{-12/13} = -\frac{13}{12} \]
  5. Sum the values with a common denominator (\(60\)):
    \[ \tan\theta + \csc\theta = \frac{12}{5} - \frac{13}{12} = \frac{144 - 65}{60} = \frac{79}{60} \]
The exact value is \(\mathbf{\frac{79}{60}}\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.B — Law of Cosines for Distance Across a Lake
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.B — Law of Cosines for Distance Across a Lake

body.en:
A surveyor at point \(C\) measures the distance to point \(A\) as \(40\) meters and to point \(B\) as \(60\) meters. The angle between the two lines of sight, \(\angle ACB\), is \(120^\circ\). What is the straight-line distance between \(A\) and \(B\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify knowns: \(a = 60\), \(b = 40\), and included angle \(C = 120^\circ\).
  2. Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C \]
  3. Substitute the values (noting \(\cos 120^\circ = -\frac{1}{2}\)):
    \[ c^2 = 60^2 + 40^2 - 2(60)(40)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \]\[ c^2 = 3600 + 1600 - (-2400) = 5200 + 2400 = 7600 \]
  4. Simplify the radical:
    \[ c = \sqrt{7600} = \sqrt{100 \cdot 4 \cdot 19} = 20\sqrt{19} \approx 87.18 \text{ meters} \]
The distance between \(A\) and \(B\) is \(\mathbf{20\sqrt{19}}\) meters.
body.ar:
A surveyor at point \(C\) measures the distance to point \(A\) as \(40\) meters and to point \(B\) as \(60\) meters. The الزاوية between the two lines of sight, \(\angle ACB\), is \(120^\circ\). What is the straight-line distance between \(A\) and \(B\)?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Identify knowns: \(a = 60\), \(b = 40\), and included الزاوية \(C = 120^\circ\).
  2. Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C \]
  3. Substitute the values (noting \(\cos 120^\circ = -\frac{1}{2}\)):
    \[ c^2 = 60^2 + 40^2 - 2(60)(40)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \]\[ c^2 = 3600 + 1600 - (-2400) = 5200 + 2400 = 7600 \]
  4. Simplify the radical:
    \[ c = \sqrt{7600} = \sqrt{100 \cdot 4 \cdot 19} = 20\sqrt{19} \approx 87.18 \text{ meters} \]
The distance between \(A\) and \(B\) is \(\mathbf{20\sqrt{19}}\) meters.

label.en: Worked Example 6.C — Law of Sines in a Non-Right Triangle
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.C — Law of Sines in a Non-Right المثلث

body.en:
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A = 30^\circ\), \(\angle B = 45^\circ\), and side \(a = 8\). Find side \(b\).

Solution: By the Law of Sines:
\[ \frac{b}{\sin 45^\circ} = \frac{8}{\sin 30^\circ} \implies b = 8 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}/2}{1/2} = \mathbf{8\sqrt{2}} \]
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (حساب المثلثات والدوال المثلثية):

label.en: Worked Example 6.D — Quadrant Sign & Pythagorean Identity
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.D — Quadrant Sign & Pythagorean المتطابقة

body.en:
If \(\sin\theta = \frac{8}{17}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi\) (Quadrant II), what is \(\tan\theta\)?

Solution: From the \(8-15-17\) right triangle, \(|\cos\theta| = \frac{15}{17}\). In Quadrant II, cosine and tangent are negative, so \(\tan\theta = \mathbf{-\frac{8}{15}}\).

question.en: In right triangle \(ABC\) with \(C = 90^\circ\), \(a = 5\), and \(c = 13\). What is the value of \(\sin A + \cos A\)?
question.ar: In right triangle \(ABC\) with \(C = 90^\circ\), \(a = 5\), and \(c = 13\). ما قيمة \(\sin A + \cos A\)?

solution.en:
By the Pythagorean theorem, the adjacent leg is \(b = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12\).
Then \(\sin A = \frac{a}{c} = \frac{5}{13}\) and \(\cos A = \frac{b}{c} = \frac{12}{13}\).
Adding them together: \(\sin A + \cos A = \frac{5 + 12}{13} = \mathbf{\frac{17}{13}}\).
solution.ar:
بتطبيق Pythagorean theorem, the adjacent leg is \(b = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12\).
Then \(\sin A = \frac{a}{c} = \frac{5}{13}\) and \(\cos A = \frac{b}{c} = \frac{12}{13}\).
Adding them together: \(\sin A + \cos A = \frac{5 + 12}{13} = \mathbf{\frac{17}{13}}\).

question.en: If \(\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II, what is the value of \(\tan\theta\)?
question.ar: إذا كان \(\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II, ما قيمة \(\tan\theta\)?

solution.en:
In Quadrant II, \(x = -4\) and hypotenuse \(r = 5\). Using \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\):
\[ (-4)^2 + y^2 = 5^2 \implies 16 + y^2 = 25 \implies y = 3 \quad (\text{positive in QII}) \]Therefore: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{3}{-4} = \mathbf{-\frac{3}{4}}\).
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: In Quadrant II, \(x = -4\) and hypotenuse \(r = 5\). Using \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\):
\[ (-4)^2 + y^2 = 5^2 \implies 16 + y^2 = 25 \implies y = 3 \quad (\text{positive in QII}) \]Therefore: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{3}{-4} = \mathbf{-\frac{3}{4}}\).

question.en: What is the period and amplitude of the trigonometric function \(f(x) = -6\cos(4x - \pi) + 3\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Trigonometry): What is the period and amplitude of the trigonometric function \(f(x) = -6\cos(4x - \pi) + 3\)?

solution.en:
For any function in standard form \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\):
  • Amplitude: \(|A| = |-6| = \mathbf{6}\).
  • Period: \(T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{\pi}{2}}\).
  • Midline: \(y = D = 3\).
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: For any function in standard form \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\):
  • Amplitude: \(|A| = |-6| = \mathbf{6}\).
  • Period: \(T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{\pi}{2}}\).
  • Midline: \(y = D = 3\).

hints.en: For any function in standard form \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\): Amplitude: \(|A| = |-6| = \mathbf{6}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\) ، \(|A| = |-6| = \mathbf{6}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{\pi}{2}}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\dfrac{1 - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\) for all values of \(\theta\) where the expression is defined?
question.ar: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\dfrac{1 - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\) for all values of \(\theta\) حيث the expression is defined?

solution.en:
Using the fundamental Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\), we have \(1 - \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta\).
Substituting this into the numerator:
\[ \frac{1 - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\cos\theta} \]
solution.ar:
باستخدام fundamental Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\), we have \(1 - \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta\).
Substituting this into the numerator:
\[ \frac{1 - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\cos\theta} \]

question.en: The function \( f(x) = a \sin(bx) + c \) has a maximum value of 9, a minimum value of \(-1\), and a period of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). If \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), what is the value of \(a + b + c\)?
question.ar: The function \( f(x) = a \sin(bx) + c \) has a maximum value of 9, a minimum value of \(-1\), and a period of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). إذا كان \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), ما قيمة \(a + b + c\)?

hints.en: To find the value of \(a + b + c\), determine each parameter from the given properties of the sinusoidal function: 1. Amplitude \(a\) and Vertical Shift \(c\):
hints.ar: To أوجد قيمة \(a + b + c\), حدّد each parameter from the given properties of the sinusoidal function: 1. Amplitude \(a\) and Vertical Shإذا كانt \(c\):

hints.en: Since \(-1 \le \sin(bx) \le 1\) and \(a > 0\), the maximum and minimum values of \(f(x)\) are: \(\text{Maximum} = c + a = 9\) \(\text{Minimum} = c - a\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(-1 \le \sin(bx) \le 1\) ، \(a > 0\) ، \(f(x)\) ، \(\text{Maximum} = c + a = 9\) ، \(\text{Minimum} = c - a\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a + b + c = 5 + 4 + 4\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
To find the value of \(a + b + c\), determine each parameter from the given properties of the sinusoidal function:

1. **Amplitude \(a\) and Vertical Shift \(c\):**
Since \(-1 \le \sin(bx) \le 1\) and \(a > 0\), the maximum and minimum values of \(f(x)\) are:
\[ \text{Maximum} = c + a = 9 \]
\[ \text{Minimum} = c - a = -1 \]

Adding these two equations gives:
\[ 2c = 8 \implies c = 4 \]

Substituting \(c = 4\) into \(c + a = 9\):
\[ 4 + a = 9 \implies a = 5 \]

2. **Frequency Parameter \(b\):**
The period \(T\) of a sine function \(\sin(bx)\) with \(b > 0\) is given by \(T = \frac{2\pi}{b}\). Setting this equal to the given period \(\frac{\pi}{2}\):
\[ \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies b\pi = 4\pi \implies b = 4 \]

3. **Sum of the Parameters:**
\[ a + b + c = 5 + 4 + 4 = 13 \]

**Common Traps:**
- Choice A (9) mistakenly calculates only \(a + c = 9\), ignoring the parameter \(b\).
- Choice B (11) mistakenly uses the tangent period formula \(\frac{\pi}{b}\), yielding \(b = 2\) and \(5 + 2 + 4 = 11\).
- Choice D (18) confuses the amplitude with the full vertical span \(9 - (-1) = 10\), leading to \(10 + 4 + 4 = 18\).
solution.ar:
To أوجد قيمة \(a + b + c\), حدّد each parameter from the given properties of the sinusoidal function:

1. **Amplitude \(a\) and Vertical Shإذا كانt \(c\):**
Since \(-1 \le \sin(bx) \le 1\) and \(a > 0\), the maximum and minimum values of \(f(x)\) are:
\[ \text{Maximum} = c + a = 9 \]
\[ \text{Minimum} = c - a = -1 \]

Adding these two equations gives:
\[ 2c = 8 \implies c = 4 \]

Substituting \(c = 4\) into \(c + a = 9\):
\[ 4 + a = 9 \implies a = 5 \]

2. **Frequency Parameter \(b\):**
The period \(T\) of a sine function \(\sin(bx)\) with \(b > 0\) is given by \(T = \frac{2\pi}{b}\). Setting this equal to the given period \(\frac{\pi}{2}\):
\[ \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies b\pi = 4\pi \implies b = 4 \]

3. **Sum of the Parameters:**
\[ a + b + c = 5 + 4 + 4 = 13 \]

**Common Traps:**
- Choice A (9) mistakenly احسبs only \(a + c = 9\), ignoring the parameter \(b\).
- Choice B (11) mistakenly uses the tangent period formula \(\frac{\pi}{b}\), yielding \(b = 2\) and \(5 + 2 + 4 = 11\).
- Choice D (18) confuses the amplitude with the full vertical span \(9 - (-1) = 10\), leading to \(10 + 4 + 4 = 18\).

label.ar: ● الدليل الشامل للنسب المثلثية الست — دائرة الوحدة والمقلوبات والمجالات والدورات وخطوط التقارب

body.en:
For any angle \( heta\) in standard position whose terminal ray intersects the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) at \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (or a right triangle with opposite \(o\), adjacent \(a\), and hypotenuse \(h\)), the six trigonometric functions are:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
FunctionDomainRangePeriodSymmetryVertical Asymptotes
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)OddNone
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)EvenNone
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Even\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)

Pythagorean Identities: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\), \(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\), and \(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).
body.ar:
لأي زاوية \( heta\) في الوضع القياسي يقطع ضلع انتهائها دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) عند النقطة \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (أو في مثلث قائم الزاوية بمقابل \(o\) ومجاور \(a\) ووتر \(h\))، تُعرَّف الدوال المثلثية الست كما يلي:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
الدالةالمجالالمدىالدورة الأساسيةالتماثلخطوط التقارب الرأسية
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)فرديةلا يوجد
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)زوجيةلا يوجد
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)زوجية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)

متطابقات فيثاغورس المثلثية: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\)، و\(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\)، و\(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).

label.en: ● All 6 Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Restricted Domains & Principal Ranges
label.ar: ● الدوال المثلثية العكسية الست جميعاً — المجالات المقيدة والمدى الأساسي

body.en:
Because the six trigonometric functions are periodic, they are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\). Restricting each forward function to its canonical principal branch makes it strictly monotonic so that a unique inverse exists (whose graph is the reflection of the restricted branch across \(y = x\)):

Inverse FunctionEquivalent StatementDomain of \(f^{-1}(x)\)Principal Range (Radians)Unit Circle Quadrants
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)Quadrants I & II

Reciprocal & Cofunction Identities: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) and \(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) for \(|x| \ge 1\); \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
body.ar:
نظراً لأن الدوال المثلثية الست دورية، فإنها ليست متباينة (واحداً لواحد) على \(\mathbb{R}\). بتقييد مجال كل دالة إلى فرعها الأساسي تصبح رتيبة تماماً وقابلة للعكس، ويكون تمثيل الدالة العكسية انعكاساً للفرع المقيّد حول المستقيم \(y = x\):

الدالة العكسيةالصيغة المكافئةمجال \(f^{-1}(x)\)المدى الأساسي (بالراديان)أرباع دائرة الوحدة
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)الربعان الأول والثاني

متطابقات المقلوبات والدوال المتممة: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) و\(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) لكل \(|x| \ge 1\)؛ وكذلك \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) و\(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
